phaseCards.title: Phase 1 Apr 18 – May 1
items: → Cover all 5 units of DSA, Chem, Math, BEEE
→ Front-load hardest subjects before hackathon
→ Light days = review only, not new content
→ Before Apr 24: photograph all notes

phaseCards.title: Phase 2 May 2 – May 8
items: → Cover Bioinformatics, CW, UHV on full days
→ First revision cycle for all 4 core subjects
→ PYQ solving begins — 2 subjects minimum
→ Build 1-page summary per subject

phaseCards.title: Phase 3 May 9 – May 10
items: → Timed mock tests (20 marks each subject)
→ Fix only identified weak areas
→ Formula sheet + keyword review only
→ No new topics after May 9 morning

phaseCards.title: Hackathon recovery strategy
items: → Apr 28: half-effort only — decompress first
→ Catch-up via pre-made notes, not re-learning
→ Hackathon nights: optional 15-min mental review
→ Keep a "where I left off" card per subject

phase1.title: Saturday, April 18
phase1.subtitle: Day 1
phase1.note: Priority: DSA deep dive (searching + sorting) + Chemistry U1

blocks.text: Plan the day, review goals, warm up. Write today's target on paper.
DSA Unit 1 — Searching: linear search, binary search. Write pseudocode + trace an example array on paper.
Break — stretch, water, no screen.
DSA Unit 2 — Sorting: bubble, selection, insertion, merge sort. Write time complexity table. Trace at least one sort by hand.
Lunch + rest (mandatory — no phone study).
Chemistry Unit 1 — Read full unit, make short bullet notes, mark key reactions/formulas.
Break — walk if possible.
DSA Revision — Make 1 algorithm card per sorting/searching method. Trace each from memory.
Daily review: what's clear? what's fuzzy? write 3 confusion points. Sleep on it.

phase1.title: Sunday, April 19
phase1.subtitle: Day 2
phase1.note: Priority: DSA completion (stack, queue, linked list) + Math U1

blocks.text: DSA Unit 3 — Stack: LIFO, push/pop/peek, applications (expression evaluation, balanced brackets), array + linked list implementation.
Break.
DSA Unit 4 — Queue: FIFO, enqueue/dequeue, circular queue, deque. Draw memory diagrams.
Lunch + rest.
DSA Unit 5 — Linked List: singly, doubly, circular. Insert/delete at head, tail, middle — trace each operation with boxes and arrows.
Break.
Mathematics Unit 1 — Read unit, solve all textbook examples (show full working). Mark formulas in a box.
DSA complete review: trace 1 algorithm for each of the 5 topics from memory. Mark confusion points.
Chemistry Unit 2 — Read + underline key concepts + reactions. Aim for coverage, not mastery.
Flashcard review: DSA Units 1+2 — name each algorithm, state its complexity in 10 seconds flat.
Mathematics Unit 2 — Read + solve 5 examples. Write formulas on a sticky note.
DSA Unit 3 review — trace stack push/pop for an expression on paper.
BEEE Unit 1 — Circuit laws: Ohm's law, KCL, KVL. Read + solve 3 numerical problems.
Chemistry Unit 1 flashcard review — key reactions from memory.

phase1.title: Thursday, April 23
phase1.subtitle: Day 6 — Last day before hackathon
phase1.note: After 1 PM only. Critical: photograph all notes today before you leave.

blocks.text: BEEE Unit 2 — AC circuits, phasors, RLC circuits. Make notes + solve 5 numericals.
Break.
BEEE Unit 3 — Transformers, semiconductor basics. Overview + key concepts only.
Pre-hackathon prep: photograph all notes. Write a "where I left off" card for each subject. Pack it with you.

phase1.title: April 24–27 (Fri–Mon)
phase1.description: No formal study sessions. Optional: 10–15 min mental review before sleeping — just flip through your "where I left off" card. Don't feel guilty. The hackathon is also building you. Come back rested on April 28.

phase1.week: Week 2 — Apr 28 – May 1 — Post-hackathon recovery + coverage finish
phase1.title: Tuesday, April 28
phase1.subtitle: Recovery day — ease back in gently
phase1.note: Don't push hard. Just re-engage the brain. 1 hour max.

blocks.text: Chemistry — Re-read your own notes for Units 1+2 only. Refresh, no new content.
Review your "where I left off" cards. Plan the next 4 days in writing.

phase1.week: Week 2 — Apr 28 – May 1 — Post-hackathon recovery + coverage finish
phase1.title: Wednesday, April 29
phase1.subtitle: Day 8

blocks.text: Chemistry Unit 3 — Read + notes. 45 minutes, no more.
Mathematics Unit 3 — Read + 3 examples. 45 minutes.

phase1.week: Week 2 — Apr 28 – May 1 — Post-hackathon recovery + coverage finish
phase1.title: Thursday, April 30
phase1.subtitle: Day 9

blocks.text: BEEE Unit 4 — Diodes, rectifiers, clipper/clamper circuits. Notes + 4 solved problems.
Break.
BEEE Unit 5 — Transistors, amplifiers, logic gates. Complete coverage. Make formula list.
Mathematics Unit 4 — Read key theorems + attempt 3 problems.

phase1.week: Week 2 — Apr 28 – May 1 — Post-hackathon recovery + coverage finish
phase1.title: Friday, May 1
phase1.subtitle: Day 10 — Phase 1 closes today

blocks.text: Chemistry Units 4+5 — Focus on mechanisms and reaction sequences. Coverage complete today.
Break.
Mathematics Unit 5 — Read + 5 examples. Math coverage complete today.
Coverage audit: mark each of the 35 units as Done / Partial / Skipped. Plan Phase 2 accordingly.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Saturday, May 2
phase2.subtitle: Day 11

blocks.text: Bioinformatics Units 1+2 — Sequence alignment, BLAST, databases. Read + notes + key diagrams.
Break.
Bioinformatics Unit 3 — Phylogenetics, genomics. Notes + draw phylogenetic tree structure.
Lunch + rest.
Computer Workshop Units 1+2 — Practical concepts, commands, key task workflows.
Break.
Chemistry — Revision cycle 1: Units 1+2+3. Use your notes only — no textbook. Rewrite unclear points.
PYQ session: 5 past Chemistry questions. Attempt without notes first, then check.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Sunday, May 3
phase2.subtitle: Day 12
phase2.note: Complete minor subjects + Math revision cycle 1

blocks.text: Bioinformatics Units 4+5 — Drug discovery, proteomics, bioinformatics applications. Full coverage.
Break.
Computer Workshop Units 3+4+5 — Remaining units. Focus on what's likely in exams (practical tasks).
Lunch + rest.
UHV Units 1+2+3 — Read through, underline key philosophical concepts, note definitions.
Break.
Mathematics — Revision cycle 1: Units 1+2+3. Redo examples without solution — check after.
PYQ session: 5 past Mathematics questions. Show all steps even for questions you struggle with.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Monday, May 4
phase2.subtitle: Day 13

blocks.text: UHV Units 4+5 — Complete coverage. Make a 1-page summary of all 5 units. Easy marks, don't over-invest.
DSA PYQ — Solve 4 past questions on searching/sorting. Trace the algorithm, don't just write the answer.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Tuesday, May 5
phase2.subtitle: Day 14

blocks.text: Chemistry — Revision cycle 1 finish: Units 4+5. Focus on reactions you couldn't recall last time.
DSA PYQ — 4 questions on stack/queue/linked list. Draw boxes and pointers, not just words.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Wednesday, May 6
phase2.subtitle: Day 15

blocks.text: Mathematics — Revision cycle 1 finish: Units 4+5. Rework problem types you got wrong. Focus on method, not answer.
Subject audit: review your Done/Partial/Skipped checklist. Flag weak spots for May 7–8.

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Thursday, May 7
phase2.subtitle: Day 16

blocks.text: BEEE — Full revision all 5 units. Minimum 3 numericals per unit. Draw circuit diagrams clearly.
Break.
Bioinformatics — Full revision all 5 units. Make 1-page visual summary. Definitions + flowcharts win here.
PYQ: 5 BEEE questions + 5 Bioinformatics questions — timed (10 min per question max).

phase2.week: Week 3 — May 2–8 — Complete minor subjects + first revision cycle
phase2.title: Friday, May 8
phase2.subtitle: Day 17 — Phase 2 closes today

blocks.text: DSA — Full revision all 5 topics. Trace 1 algorithm per topic from scratch. Write time/space complexity.
Computer Workshop + UHV — Quick skim of your 1-page summaries. Identify likely questions.
Break.
Build your "Last 2 Days Cheat Sheet" — 1 A4 page per subject. Only what you keep forgetting. This is your exam-day lifeline.

phase3.week: May 9–10 — Final mock tests and last revision
phase3.title: Saturday, May 9
phase3.subtitle: Day 18 — Simulate the exam
phase3.note: Timed mock conditions. No notes during the attempt — check only after.

blocks.text: Chemistry Mock — Attempt 20 marks of PYQ under timed conditions. Mark yourself strictly.
Chemistry review — note every error type. Don't re-read full units. Patch only the gaps.
Break.
Mathematics Mock — 20 marks PYQ. Check step-by-step. Part marks matter — show all work.
Lunch + rest (mandatory).
BEEE Mock — 20 marks. Mix of numericals and theory. Draw diagrams for full marks.
Break.
DSA Mock — Trace 2 algorithms from scratch + answer 3 theory questions without notes.
Error analysis — make a "weak points only" list per subject. This becomes your May 10 morning checklist.

phase3.week: May 9–10 — Final mock tests and last revision
phase3.title: Sunday, May 10
phase3.subtitle: Day 19 — Last day before exams
phase3.note: No new topics today. Fix known gaps only. Brain off by 9 PM.

blocks.text: Chemistry + Mathematics — Address May 9 weak points only. Use cheat sheets, not full notes.
BEEE + DSA — Fix gaps from mock. Re-attempt 2 problems you got wrong yesterday.
Bioinformatics + Computer Workshop + UHV — Final skim of 1-page summaries only.
Lunch + rest (mandatory).
Read all cheat sheets one final time. Don't write — just read and let it consolidate.
Walk, relax, light music. No study at all.
Optional: reattempt 2–3 problems you couldn't solve before. Light confidence boost only.
Pack exam bag. Lay out everything. Sleep by 10 PM. Memory consolidates during sleep — trust it.

phase3.week: May 9–10 — Final mock tests and last revision
phase3.title: Monday, May 11 onwards
phase3.description: On each exam morning: review your 1-page cheat sheet only. Eat a proper meal. Arrive 10 minutes early. In the exam: attempt all questions, show all working, define before explaining. You've done the work — trust it.

cards.title: Deep work session structure
items: → Ideal block: 90–100 min, no phone, no interruptions
→ Full days: 2 blocks AM + 2 blocks PM (max 4 blocks)
→ Half days: 1 block + 1 shorter block (60–75 min)
→ Light days: 1 block only, low pressure, no guilt
→ Break between blocks: 15–20 min hard limit
→ Never study 2 similar subjects back to back

cards.title: PYQ timing strategy
items: → DSA: May 4–5 (after full coverage + 1 week gap)
→ Chemistry: May 2 + May 5 (during revision)
→ Mathematics: May 3 + May 6
→ BEEE: May 7
→ Bio / CW / UHV: May 7–8
→ Rule: always attempt without notes first, then check

cards.title: 3-cycle revision system
items: → Cycle 1 — Coverage (Apr 18–May 1): first read, rough notes
→ Cycle 2 — Compression (May 2–8): notes → 1-page summaries
→ Cycle 3 — Triggers (May 9–10): summaries → keywords only
→ Each cycle should take 40% less time than the previous one

cards.title: The 40/50 scoring formula
items: → 5 units × ~8 marks = 40. Coverage beats perfection.
→ Know 1–2 "anchor questions" per unit — guaranteed marks
→ Learn all definitions — 1–2 marks each, easy to get
→ Math/BEEE: show working even if answer is wrong (part marks)
→ DSA: trace examples with diagrams — examiner loves diagrams
→ Bio/UHV: keywords in answers = higher marks, even if vague

cards.title: Daily tracking system
items: → Each morning: write today's 1 priority target on paper
→ Each evening: mark units as Done / Partial / Skipped
→ Rate each study session: 1–5 (energy × output)
→ Every Sunday: recalibrate next week's plan based on what's pending
→ Backlog rule: never carry more than 1 item to the next day

cards.title: Burnout prevention rules
items: → Never study past 10 PM — sleep is the final revision
→ One guilt-free hour per day (non-study, any activity)
→ If exhausted: 20-min nap beats 60 min of bad study
→ Progress over perfection — 6 units covered > 2 units perfect
→ Don't compare pace with others — you have different constraints

subjectTactics.subject: DSA
subjectTactics.body: Trace every algorithm on paper. Draw array boxes for searching/sorting. Draw linked nodes with arrows. Never just read — always trace with a pencil.

subjectTactics.subject: Chemistry
subjectTactics.body: Reactions + mechanisms are most of the marks. Make a master reaction sheet. Read it every night before bed. 10 key reactions per unit minimum.

subjectTactics.subject: Mathematics
subjectTactics.body: Practice problems, not theory reading. At least 5 problems per topic. Show every step in exam — method marks are real even when answer is wrong.

subjectTactics.subject: BEEE
subjectTactics.body: Numericals = guaranteed marks. Solve at least 3 per sub-topic. Always draw the circuit diagram. Label everything — examiners give marks for labeled diagrams.

subjectTactics.subject: Bioinformatics
subjectTactics.body: Mostly theory and definitions. One-page visual summary per unit with a flowchart. Write answers using subject-specific vocabulary — it signals you know the topic.

subjectTactics.subject: UHV
subjectTactics.body: 1-credit subject — don't over-invest. 4 hours total is the ceiling. Learn 3 probable long-answer questions and 10 definitions. That's enough for a good score.

fallback.title: Fallen behind by 1–2 days
items: → Don't try to catch everything at once — pick the highest-credit subject and cover that unit first
→ Compress 2 units into one session: skim reading + key notes only (no deep examples)
→ Downgrade UHV and Computer Workshop to "notes skim only" — buys you 3–4 hours back
→ Use next full day (Sat/Sun) as a dedicated catch-up block before moving forward

fallback.title: Fallen behind by 3–5 days
items: → Drop revision cycle 2 for UHV and Computer Workshop — 1 read is enough for those subjects
→ Use May 9 as an emergency coverage day for incomplete subjects instead of a mock day
→ Priority order: DSA → Chemistry → Mathematics → BEEE → Bioinformatics → CW → UHV
→ Minimum viable target: 3 units fully covered + 2 units skimmed = still achievable 30–35 per subject

fallback.title: Emergency last-48-hours protocol
items: → Read ONLY your self-made notes — no textbooks, no YouTube, no new sources
→ Per topic: 1 definition + 1 formula + 1 example. That's the minimum viable unit.
→ DSA: memorize algorithm steps in plain English — examiner gives marks for structured answers
→ Chemistry: master 10 key reactions per unit — even partially written reactions score
→ Math/BEEE: practice 2 numericals per unit — method + diagram = most of the marks
→ Skip anything you haven't started — sunk cost. Strengthen what you know. That's the play.

fallback.title: Daily backlog check — every evening
items: → Ask yourself: "Did I hit today's target?" Yes = great. No = note exactly what's pending.
→ Carry over only 1 item to tomorrow — don't create a snowball of tasks
→ If 3+ items are piling up: declare a "catch-up Saturday" and clear everything in one block
→ The rule: no backlog survives past the next full day. If it does, drop the lowest-priority item entirely.
